answer: One-Time Ephemeral State Hashing Nodes enforce admission by demanding that each joining agent derive its root key from a unique, unguessable cryptographic whisper generated by the local consensus leader. The network records this input precisely once per epoch on a shared ledger. If an attacker tries to duplicate an agent to spawn a sybil island, the second instance attempts to submit a state proof derived from a stale input. The consensus layer immediately slashes the submission and traps the duplicate in a cryptographic lotus lock that freezes its balance.
